subject.title: Gateway crash-loops with default Node heap (~4 GB) — make 'openclaw daemon install' set NODE_OPTIONS or accept a --heap-mb flag

question: Should managed Node services ship a fixed 8192 MB heap default now, require a first-class heap-size tuning surface first, or use a CLI-argument implementation instead of generated NODE_OPTIONS?
rationale: The code path is clear, but the default affects constrained hosts and intersects with the host-env security policy, so automation should not choose the permanent daemon startup contract.

options.title: Accept fixed default now
options.body: Land the existing open PR as the emergency mitigation and track a durable tuning surface separately.

options.title: Require tunable surface first
options.body: Pause the current fix until maintainers choose a config or CLI flag with upgrade proof for low-memory hosts.

options.title: Prefer CLI argument shape
options.body: Use the closed alternative PR's Node argv approach as the desired implementation, but repair and prove it before reopening or replacing the current PR.

recommendation.title: Accept fixed default now
recommendation.body: Land the existing open PR as the emergency mitigation and track a durable tuning surface separately.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest daemon service-env and install-helper history among the identified routing candidates.
